summary.text: Michael Allen, a Republican and the elected District Attorney for Colorado's 4th Judicial District, lost the November 3, 2026 election for attorney general of Colorado to Jena Griswold.
A U.S. Navy veteran and career prosecutor, he was first elected district attorney in 2020 and re-elected in 2024.
His campaign centered on public safety, consumer protection, water rights and accountability in government.

paragraphs.text: Allen is a Colorado native who grew up in the Denver area and enlisted in the U.S. Navy after high school.
His campaign says he served eight years in the Navy as an Aviation Electronics Technician.
He later earned an undergraduate degree from the University of Northern Colorado and a law degree from the University of Kansas.
Allen has worked in prosecution for more than 20 years, beginning as a law-school intern in 2004.
Early in his career he prosecuted consumer-protection cases in the Kansas Attorney General's Office.
He was elected District Attorney for the 4th Judicial District, which covers El Paso and Teller counties and is the state's largest judicial district, in 2020 and re-elected in 2024.
He has also served as president of the Colorado District Attorneys' Council.
As district attorney, Allen's campaign says he created an Organized Crime Unit and launched a motor vehicle theft team, and that his office prosecuted the Club Q shooting case as a hate crime.
He defeated David Willson in the Republican primary on June 30, 2026, and faced Democrat Jena Griswold in the general election.
Allen and his wife, Heidi, have been married for more than 30 years and have two sons.
He received 41% of the vote to Jena Griswold's 59%, according to unofficial results reported by NBC News.
